cases.summary: PCIe replay counter on GPU 1 rose from 176 to 505 in 3 minutes (160-170 per minute), while all other GPUs on the node showed zero PCIe replays. GPU 1 operated at normal temperature (62-65°C) with no throttling, and power limit was at default 400W (not capped). The issue is isolated to GPU 1's PCIe path. This matches the pattern of PCIe link degradation, typically caused by a riser not fully seated or degraded PCIe cable to the retimer.
cases.rationale: Runbook recommends draining the node when PCIe replays are detected, as they often precede a GPU falling off the bus. This allows for reseating the GPU and riser/cable during maintenance, which resolved similar incidents in the past.

cases.summary: GPUs 4, 5, 6 on a6test-a100-node-03 show thermal runaway: thermal residual alerts (+12-13°C hotter than power predicts), z-score temperature alerts (z=+5.6 to +6.6), static threshold violations (84-86°C), and thermal throttling. All three GPUs are affected simultaneously, with elevated temperatures and throttled samples while power limits remain at default 400W (not power-capped). No ECC, PCIe, or NVLink errors. This pattern matches historical incidents where fan module failures caused thermal runaway on adjacent GPUs.
cases.rationale: Thermal runaway detected on GPUs 4-6 with thermal residual alerts, elevated temperatures, and thermal throttling. Runbooks indicate this is typically a fan failure requiring node drain followed by fan module replacement. Drain node to stop new jobs and allow safe hot-swap of the failed fan.

cases.summary: GPU 7 on node a6test-h100-node-01 showed clear ECC degradation: SBE errors rose from ~3 to 269 over the incident window, with multiple retired pages events (ev-60, ev-85, ev-104). A burst of SBE errors occurred (ev-87, ev-88, ev-89). XID 48 (DBE - Double Bit Error) was recorded at 05:38:54Z, followed by ecc_dbe_total threshold crossing (ev-140). Power limit remained at default 700W (not power-capped), temperatures were elevated (~60-70°C) but not at thermal slowdown limits. Neighboring GPUs had similar thermal profiles but no ECC issues. This matches the ecc_degradation pattern: rising SBE, retired pages, culminating in DBE/XID 48.
cases.rationale: Per runbook rb-002-ecc-degradation#remediation: DBE/XID 48 occurred, job lost. Drain node at next safe point, then reset GPU to apply pending row remaps. If errors resume after reset, RMA the GPU.

cases.summary: GPU 1 on node a6test-a100-node-02 fell off the bus at 2026-09-30T04:45:54Z. Evidence: XID 79 (GPU off bus), BMC PCIe fatal error on slot 1, and GPU 1 stopped reporting samples. Telemetry shows GPU was operating normally until failure (power ~371W, temp ~65°C, util ~90%, power limit at 400W default). No rising error counters. Pattern matches past gpu_off_bus incidents with root causes being hardware faults (PCIe riser, GPU) or driver issues.
cases.rationale: Runbook for gpu_off_bus indicates hardware replacement (GPU or PCIe riser) after XID 79 and PCIe fatal error. Past incidents resolved by replacing faulty components.

cases.summary: GPU 5 on node a6test-a100-node-01 fell off the bus at 2026-09-30T05:17:04Z. Evidence: (1) XID 79 logged by GPU driver indicating "GPU has fallen off the bus", (2) BMC critical PCIe fatal error on GPU slot 5, (3) GPU 5 stopped reporting telemetry samples after the event while other GPUs continued normal operation. The failure pattern matches known gpu_off_bus incidents where a GPU disconnects from the PCIe bus, typically due to hardware fault (GPU or riser). No prior rising error counters (ECC, PCIe replay, NVLink CRC) were observed, and neighboring GPUs operated normally, confirming this was an isolated GPU failure.
cases.rationale: The runbook for gpu_off_bus failures indicates that when a GPU falls off the bus (XID 79 + PCIe fatal error), the hardware (GPU or riser) needs to be replaced. This is a hardware fault requiring physical replacement, not a transient issue that can be resolved by reset or monitoring.

cases.summary: NVLink degradation detected on GPUs 0 and 1 of a6test-h100-node-04. Evidence: (1) NVLink CRC errors rose from 0 to 4373 on GPU 0 and 0 to 4155 on GPU 1 between 12:50-13:33, with both GPUs sharing an NVLink connection. (2) XID 74 logged on GPU 0 at 13:17:44Z confirming "NVLink Error. Link 3 CRC errors." (3) Both GPUs showed correlated behavior: power dropped from ~670-680W to ~500-550W, temperature from ~69-70°C to ~59-61°C, and utilization from ~90-97% to ~67-75% around 12:50-12:54. (4) Neighbor GPUs 3-7 remained healthy with stable NVLink CRC counters and no errors. This matches the nvlink_degradation pattern: rising NVLink CRC errors on two GPUs sharing a link, XID 74, and correlated performance degradation.
cases.rationale: Runbook rb-005-nvlink-degradation indicates NVLink degradation requires draining the node and resetting all GPUs on the baseboard. Past incidents (inc-2025025, inc-2025004) show this resolved link training issues. Drain node for human approval before baseboard reset.

cases.summary: NVLink degradation confirmed on GPUs 2 and 3 of node a6test-a100-node-02. Evidence: (1) Rising NVLink CRC error counters on both GPUs (~4100-4200 increase over the window); (2) XID 74 "NVLINK Error. Link 3 CRC errors" logged on GPU 2 at 13:44:24Z; (3) Both GPUs show reduced utilization (~80-81%) compared to neighbors (~92-94%), consistent with NVLink slowdown. No other fault signals present (no thermal, power, PCIe, or ECC errors). The detector's suspected failure type is correct.
cases.rationale: Runbook recommends draining the node for NVLink degradation as degraded links slow every job that uses them. This allows time for link retraining or hardware service if errors persist after reboot.

cases.summary: PCIe replay counter on GPU 5 of a6test-a100-node-02 is rising steadily (137→205→260 over 10-min windows, ~67 replays/min). Only GPU 5 shows this pattern; all other GPUs (0-4, 6-7) have zero PCIe replay increase. Power limit is at default 400W (not power-capped), temperature is normal (~60-65°C), no throttling, no ECC errors, no NVLink CRC errors. This isolated PCIe replay pattern on a single GPU points to a PCIe path issue (cable, riser, or retimer) rather than node-wide or thermal/power issues. Similar past incidents show degraded PCIe cables to retimers as root cause.
cases.rationale: Runbook rb-006-pcie-degradation#remediation states: "Replays without errors are not urgent, but they often come before a GPU falls off the bus. Schedule a drain." This is a PCIe degradation incident requiring node drain to prevent potential GPU off-bus failure, followed by reseating/replacing the riser or cable during maintenance.

cases.summary: All 8 GPUs on a6test-h100-node-03 show enforced power limit reduced to 420 W (nominal 700 W for H100). This node-wide power cap is the key signal. No error counters (ECC, PCIe replay, NVLink CRC) are rising. BMC/XID logs are empty (common, doesn't rule out hardware). The pattern matches known PSU failure incidents where a PSU module failure triggers the power management system to cap power across all GPUs. The z-score evidence for GPU 7 shows "consistent with the GPU's power" - meaning the low power reading is expected given the power cap, not a workload shift.
cases.rationale: Runbook for power_fault indicates PSU failure causes node-wide power capping. Resolution is hot-swapping the failed PSU from spares. No drain needed for PSU swap on redundant chassis.

cases.summary: GPU 6 on a6test-a100-node-02 shows clear ECC degradation: SBE count rose from 5 to 327+ over ~4.5 hours, with 3 retired page events and a DBE (uncorrectable error) with XID 48 at 2026-10-01T01:35:44Z. The node summary confirms ecc_sbe_increase=327 and ecc_dbe_increase=1 for GPU 6, while all other GPUs had near-zero increases. Temperatures (~65°C avg) and power (~379W avg) are normal, with power limit at default 400W. No PCIe replay or NVLink CRC errors. This matches the ecc_degradation pattern: rising SBE, retired pages, ending in DBE/XID 48.
cases.rationale: Runbook rb-002-ecc-degradation#remediation states: "DBE / XID 48 occurred: the job on that GPU is lost. Drain, reset, and check for a remapping failure." Drain node to stop scheduling new jobs on GPU 6, then reset GPU to apply pending row remaps. If errors resume or remapping fails, RMA the GPU.

cases.summary: PSU1 on node a6test-h100-node-01 failed at 2026-09-30T21:21:14Z, as evidenced by BMC warning "Input lost" error. This caused the system to enforce a reduced power limit of 420W (below the 700W default for H100 GPUs) across all GPUs on the node. Multiple GPUs (3, 5, 7) triggered power_limit_reduced events showing 420W enforced vs 700W nominal. The pattern matches known PSU failure incidents where power capping occurs across all GPUs. No other fault signals (thermal, ECC, PCIe, NVLink) were present.
cases.rationale: PSU1 failed as evidenced by BMC "Input lost" error. Runbooks indicate PSU failures require hot-swapping the failed PSU module. No drain needed as PSU swap is hot-swappable on redundant chassis.

cases.summary: GPU 6 on a6test-h100-node-03 shows steadily rising PCIe replay counters (376→622→909 over 3 consecutive 10-min windows, total increase of 5163 in the metrics window). The power limit is at default 700W (not power-capped), no thermal throttling, no ECC errors, and no NVLink errors. Other GPUs on the same node show no PCIe replays. This pattern matches PCIe degradation symptoms from the runbook.
cases.rationale: Runbook recommends draining for PCIe degradation as replays often precede GPU falling off the bus. Schedule drain to allow maintenance window for reseating GPU/riser/cable.

cases.summary: GPU 3 on a6test-a100-node-03 shows clear ECC degradation pattern: SBE errors rose from 5 to 286 over ~3 hours, retired_pages_total reached 1 (page retirement), burst of 50-51 SBE errors occurred, XID 48 (DBE double-bit ECC error) appeared at 04:23:04Z, and ecc_dbe_total reached 1. The node summary confirms GPU 3 is the only GPU with significant ECC increases (278 SBE, 1 DBE) while neighbors show 0 increase. Temperature and power are normal (62-66°C, 364-393W, 400W limit), ruling out thermal or power issues. This matches the ecc_degradation pattern of rising SBE → page retirement → DBE/XID 48 indicating degrading HBM stack.
cases.rationale: Runbook rb-002-ecc-degradation#remediation states: "Rising SBE rate, no DBE yet: drain the node at the next safe point... reset the GPU so pending row remaps take effect... If errors resume after the reset, RMA the GPU." Since XID 48 (DBE) already occurred, drain the node, reset GPU 3 to apply pending row remaps, and monitor. If errors resume within 2 days, RMA the GPU per inc-2025015#report lessons.

cases.summary: GPU 4 on a6test-a100-node-01 fell off the bus at 2026-10-01T02:20:04Z. Evidence: (1) XID 79 from GPU driver indicating GPU fell off the bus; (2) BMC critical PCIe fatal error on GPU slot 4; (3) GPU 4 stopped reporting telemetry (samples=0) while all other GPUs continued normal operation. This matches the gpu_off_bus failure pattern. No error counter rises (ECC, PCIe replay, NVLink CRC all zero) and no thermal/power anomalies. Similar incidents show root causes are typically faulty PCIe riser or GPU hardware fault.
cases.rationale: GPU 4 has fallen off the bus (XID 79 + BMC PCIe fatal error), requiring immediate drain to stop scheduling jobs on the affected node. Per runbook, drain the node when a GPU falls off the bus to prevent job failures.

cases.summary: GPU 6 on a6test-a100-node-03 shows rising correctable ECC errors (SBE) from 3 to 9 over the investigation window, with threshold breaches at 10:59, 11:00, and 11:01 (5 errors in 30 min). No XID errors logged, no power cap (power limit at 400W default), no thermal issues (temps 63-64°C similar to neighbors), no PCIe or NVLink errors. Pattern matches ecc_degradation - degrading HBM memory. Other GPUs on node are healthy with no ECC errors.
cases.rationale: Runbook for ecc_degradation recommends draining the node at the next safe point and resetting the GPU to apply pending row remaps. This allows the system to clear any pending remaps and assess if errors resume. If errors resume after reset, RMA the GPU.

cases.summary: GPU 5 on a6test-h100-node-01 experienced XID 79 (GPU fell off the bus) at 2026-10-01T10:08:54Z, followed by complete loss of telemetry (samples=0) from 10:11:00Z. The GPU was under heavy load (98% utilization, 683W power, 71.6°C max temp) with 105 throttled samples before failure. No power cap (power_limit=700W default), no thermal residual, and no rising error counters (ECC, PCIe replay, NVLink CRC all zero). The XID 79 is a definitive hardware fault signal indicating the GPU fell off the PCIe bus.
cases.rationale: Runbook rb-004-gpu-off-bus#remediation requires draining the node after XID 79, as the GPU cannot be recovered while the OS is running. A reboot will be needed after drain approval; GPU reset alone is insufficient.

cases.summary: Four GPUs (0-3) on node a6test-a100-node-02 show thermal runaway. All four GPUs have thermal_residual evidence of 14-15°C hotter than their power draw predicts (ev-0, ev-1, ev-2). All exceeded 83°C static threshold (ev-3, ev-11, ev-14) and show thermal_throttle (ev-5, ev-8, ev-17). Z-scores are +6.3 to +6.6, indicating temperatures 6+ standard deviations above historical baseline. GPUs 0-3 are in the same cooling zone and all hot, while GPUs 4-7 (neighbours) run at similar utilization (90-94%) but stay cool (63-65°C). No ECC/PCIe/NVLink errors. Pattern matches thermal_runaway: multiple GPUs in one cooling zone hot, temperatures 14+°C above power prediction, thermal throttling active. Likely failed chassis fan or blocked airflow affecting the cooling zone for GPUs 0-3.
cases.rationale: Runbook rb-001-thermal-runaway#remediation states to drain the node before replacing a fan. Running at thermal slowdown risks job timeouts and long-term GPU wear. The node should be drained to stop scheduling new jobs while the fan issue is investigated and resolved.

cases.summary: NVLink degradation on GPUs 6 and 7 of a6test-h100-node-04. Evidence: (1) NVLink CRC error counters climbed from 0 to ~4487 (GPU 6) and ~4460 (GPU 7) over ~70 minutes, exceeding thresholds (ev-0, ev-1, ev-2). (2) XID 74 logged on GPU 6 at 12:03:54Z indicating NVLink error on Link 3. (3) Both GPUs 6 and 7 are adjacent and share an NVLink connection - both affected consistently. (4) No other fault signals: power limits at default 700W (not power-capped), temperatures normal (60-63°C), no thermal throttling, no ECC/PCIe errors. This matches the nvlink_degradation pattern. Similar incidents (inc-2025032, inc-2025025, inc-2025004) show root cause is link training issue or faulty NVSwitch port, resolved by baseboard reset.
cases.rationale: Runbook rb-005-nvlink-degradation#remediation states: "Drain the node; degraded links slow every job that uses them." Followed by resetting the baseboard to retrain links. Drain is required before reset to avoid job failures during the procedure.
